items.item: An early firing isn't a lesser or buggy version of the on-time answer — it's a deliberate, labeled trade of certainty for latency, and a consumer that treats it as final is making an error the system never promised to prevent.

items.item: Allowed lateness being bounded rather than infinite isn't a limitation to work around — it's the only thing that keeps a windowed job's state from growing forever, which is exactly why the prior topic's pane-cleanup mechanics depend on it.

items.item: Calling a sum-of-sums consumer 'naive' under accumulating mode isn't a criticism of the consumer's code — the consumer is doing exactly what summing means; the mismatch is entirely about which contract the upstream job actually promised.

items.item: A retraction fixing a naive downstream sum isn't a coincidence of this topic's toy model — it's the general mechanism changelog-stream systems (Flink SQL's dynamic tables among them) use to let a simple consumer stay simple while the upstream mode gets more sophisticated.
